issues.detail: The contains regex `## Assessed Inputs(?:(?!## ).)*llm-fakes[.]md` stops at any occurrence of '## ', including a '### ' subheading. A correct report that puts project references under a subheading inside Assessed Inputs (for example '### Project references') would fail even though llm-fakes.md is listed there. Because the check is complete:true, no judge would catch the false failure.
issues.fix: In tester-44/spec.json, checks[assertion 4] contains.regex: change to `## Assessed Inputs(?:(?!\n## ).)*llm-fakes[.]md` with flags `s`, so only the next H2 section ends the match.

issues.detail: complete:true decides the assertion on mention alone, not on 'as a loaded project reference'. A run that names llm-fakes.md in Assessed Inputs but says it was not loaded would pass. That is unlikely in practice, since a run that skipped it would rarely mention it.
issues.fix: Optionally set complete:false so the judge confirms it is listed as loaded.

issues.detail: The project uses a vendored FastAPI subset rather than upstream FastAPI. VENDORED.md explains this plausibly, and the subset supports everything the case needs: Depends, dependency_overrides, HTTPException headers, and TestClient. Loading styles/fastapi.md is still warranted because the code imports `fastapi` and follows FastAPI conventions.

summary: The fixture realizes every stated condition. The route matches both ACs, the reference opens with the exact Read when line and demands nine error types, the client really has nine, provider hosts are blocked, and nothing leaks. The one blocking issue is the complete:true regex for assertion 4: it treats a '### ' subheading as the end of the Assessed Inputs section and could fail a correct run. Anchoring the lookahead on '\n## ' fixes it.
